beats.text: A first launch opens setup in the Valet window.
Step 1: where the Woolworths password comes from. Valet keeps a Keychain copy of a 1Password item.
Step 2: approve the Woolworths adapter: the sites it reaches and what each tool can do.
The review shows the adapter’s code and permissions before anything runs.
Step 3: which login to use. Choosing an item asks 1Password.
1Password asks first: unlock it, then allow Valet.
Pick the login. It may only be typed into the shop’s sign-in page.
The shop texts a code at sign-in, so Valet may read that code from Messages.
Step 4: the store whose prices and pickup times you shop with.
Step 5: connect Claude. Each app gets its own access, and the setup to copy.
Valet is set up. It lives in the menu bar from here.
Six places in the sidebar. Needs you comes first: anything waiting on you.
Sites: every site Valet can work on, and how each is doing.
Each site has its own page: what it is doing, and whether it’s healthy.
Tools: what agents can ask of this site, with what each one is allowed to change.
Permissions: its login, its codes, and its store, each with its own grant.
Versions: which adapter version is approved, and any update waiting for review.
Activity: every call an agent made, newest first.
Open a call to see each step Valet took on the site, and what it sent back.
The audit log: a hash-chained record of everything, logins and approvals included.
Search finds any place, site, call or setting: ⌘K.
…and takes you straight there.
Connections: the apps and agents that can call Valet, each with its own access.
Secrets: where each login comes from. Valet shows which, never the password.
Settings: notifications, data kept, updates, and reset.
The menu bar panel: today’s calls, each site, and the stop buttons, without opening the window.
When a site needs you to sign in yourself, Valet opens its page under a banner that says why.
Needs you shows it too, until it’s done.
Pause Valet stops every call at once. Lock down goes further.
Locked down: every call is refused, with an answer that says why, until you unlock.
Unlock puts it back. Cloud agents removed by Lock down have to be approved again.
An adapter update waits for you. Until then, that site’s tools are off.
The review compares it with the version you approved, and highlights what changed.
Approved. Logins don’t carry over to a new version, so choose it again.
The site is back on, at the new version.
A tool that can’t be undone asks you first, in a window of its own. (A test build here: no MVP Woolworths tool asks.)
The agent is told you declined, and Activity records it.
